- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.  
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) reversals; apply 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid overreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or bearish, apply 1–2% downward bias to avoid over-optimism.
